auth.apple.disclosure:
⚠️ Not officially supported by Apple. The two tokens you're about to paste belong to Apple's web player (music.apple.com):
  · Apple may change or revoke them at any time, and then they stop working — just run capy auth login apple again
  · Accessing Apple Music with a third-party tool is at your own risk under Apple's terms of service
  · capy only shows you how to copy them by hand; it never reads your browser's data
  · When capy writes, tracks added to a playlist may also be added to your Apple Music library (depending on your Apple Music settings; this is Apple's behavior); capy only writes to playlists you created

auth.apple.guide:
Copy the tokens from Apple's web player (about 1 minute):
  1. Open https://music.apple.com in a browser and log in
  2. Open DevTools (F12 / ⌥⌘I) → Network tab, filter by "amp-api"
  3. Click any song or playlist, then click any amp-api request → Request Headers
  4. Copy the value of authorization (the whole string; with or without "Bearer ") → developer token
  5. Copy the value of media-user-token → user token

auth.spotify.app_steps:
Spotify's policy limits each app to 5 users, so you need your own app:
1. Open https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard
2. Create app, any name
3. Redirect URI (copy it exactly): http://127.0.0.1:8888/callback
4. Tick Web API → Save
5. Copy the Client ID into the next field

cmd.drive.init.flag.dry_run: only list the files to create, don't upload (exits 2 if there is anything to create)
cmd.drive.init.flag.from_local: restore the files missing on Drive from this machine's state.db (currently the only mode)
cmd.drive.init.long:
The way out after pl pull stops with exit 3 because Drive is incomplete. Only creates the files missing on Drive and never overwrites existing ones (files still on Drive win),
and leaves the local cache alone; other devices' dev__ files are not uploaded on their behalf (each device writes only its own; the next time that device pulls, it has no base and only adds, never removes).
First lists the files to create (without a TTY: headerless TSV with columns action, file) and uploads only after you confirm; exit 0 = done or nothing missing, 1 = error, 2 = pending (--dry-run, no TTY without --yes, or cancelled).
The confirmation shows the Google account you are logged in to: if it's the wrong account, this command would upload all your playlist data (playlists and track mappings) to someone else's appdata.
cmd.drive.init.short: Restore the files missing from the Drive appdata using this machine's state.db (the only command allowed to write while the appdata is empty or incomplete)
cmd.drive.short: Maintenance commands for the Google Drive appdata
cmd.export.long:
Reads only the local state.db and never touches Drive, the network or the keychain. Prints one JSON object: the keys are the file names on Drive (manifest.json, tracks.json,
pl__<pid>.json, dev__<device_id>.json) and the values are those files' contents, byte-for-byte the same as on Drive. The output is the same with or without a TTY.
With no local data it exits 1 and prints nothing to stdout (so capy export > backup.json never silently writes an empty file).
cmd.export.short: Print this machine's canonical data to stdout (the Drive files merged into one JSON; an escape hatch that doesn't depend on Drive)
cmd.history.clear.short: Clear recent history (the playlist cache is kept)
cmd.history.short: Recent searches and plays (local cache, used by completion and the picker)
cmd.prev.short: Go back to the previous track
cmd.root.flag.port: port for --web (default 0 = any free port; 8888, 80 and 443 are not allowed)
cmd.root.flag.web: use capy from your browser: binds to 127.0.0.1 only and prints a one-time URL at startup
cmd.root.short: Cross-platform music CLI: search, playback control, playlist sync
cmd.update.flag.dev: update to the latest commit on main (built from source; needs the Go toolchain)
cmd.update.long:
Update capy itself.

With no flags: asks GitHub Releases for the latest release, downloads this platform's file, verifies its SHA-256
against checksums.txt and runs the new binary's --version to make sure it works, and only then replaces the running
binary. The checksum only proves the download is complete (releases are not signed).
Running it from a dev build (built with go install or --dev) switches you to the release.

--dev: asks GitHub for the latest commit on the main branch, rebuilds from source with go install, then replaces the
running binary (needs the Go toolchain; the first run downloads dependencies, about 20 seconds).
cmd.update.short: Update capy itself (latest release; --dev builds the latest commit on main)

google.guide:
Create your own Google OAuth client (free, about 5 minutes) — this binary has no built-in client (builds from go install never include one):
  1. https://console.cloud.google.com → create a project → APIs & Services → enable "Google Drive API"
  2. Google Auth platform → Branding: fill in the app name and support email; for Audience choose External
  3. Data Access: add only these three scopes — openid, userinfo.email, drive.appdata (adding Gmail or similar triggers a security assessment)
  4. Create an OAuth client of type "Desktop app"; the secret is shown only once, when it's created, so copy it right away
  5. ⚠️ Under Audience, click "Publish app" to move to In production — if it stays in Testing, the refresh token expires after 7 days and you'll be logged out without warning
  6. Paste the Client ID and Client secret below
